reason: Frozen successor-v11 Final RC/UAT PR #950 exact head ca2e8ba3cc900c24111476ea459650cec45991a8 / Product Final 33221931040 passed the first exact packaged post-install launch, frozen Element reproducibility and Matrix UAT, then failed only in the startup-capsule second packaged process with STARTUP_CAPSULE_POST_INSTALL_TIMEOUT. Existing diagnostics prove that second process reached runtime-identity-verified, acquired the LEGACY_CREDENTIAL_MIGRATION application lease, observed backend-not-owned, entered OWNER_RECOVERING with owner-recovery-not-required, and immediately became UNAVAILABLE with WP4_CREDENTIAL_OWNER_EXIT_RECOVERY_FAILED before backend spawn. Trusted-main source audit closes the prior #946 assumption: a fresh CredentialVaultHost does not restore activeOwnerSession/pendingOwnerSession from disk, initialization and lease acquisition prove lifecycle/transaction recovery completed, and no backend is owned; therefore DesktopCredentialApplicationCoordinator._assertOwnerReleased() can only reject this observed boundary through its unrelated authority.available === true predicate. That predicate conflates credential decryptability with owner-release safety. The same source audit also proves recoverCredentialVaults() is internally inconsistent: it intends to replace unreadable destination refs but first calls all-or-nothing entries(), so one unreadable ref aborts before per-ref recovery. The clean Product Final path has one runtime credential before the capsule and main provisions the system-owned Graphiti Neo4j ref before backend startup; authorize one causal batch that separates owner-release assertions from vault readability, performs per-ref legacy recovery, and allows only the exact rotatable Graphiti Neo4j system credential to be regenerated on decrypt/corruption while preserving fail-closed secure-storage behavior for all user credentials.

provenGap: The startup capsule is a fresh Electron process over the copied secure profile produced by the already-passing first packaged launch.
Fresh CredentialVaultHost construction starts with no activeOwnerSession or pendingOwnerSession, and those in-memory fields are not restored by _loadActiveAuthority().
Successful application lease acquisition proves CredentialVaultHost initialization and lifecycle recovery completed before _assertOwnerReleased().
The observed backend-not-owned transition proves backend ownership is not the rejecting predicate.
At this exact boundary, _assertOwnerReleased() incorrectly requires authority.available === true even though credential decryptability is not an owner-release invariant.
recoverCredentialVaults() calls all-or-nothing destination entries() before its intended per-ref unreadable replacement logic, so an unreadable copied credential cannot reach recovery.

The clean packaged path reaches backend hydration with exactly one credential reference and main provisions the system-owned Graphiti Neo4j credential before backend startup; that exact generated ref is rotatable, while arbitrary user credentials are not.
repair: Keep _assertOwnerReleased() strict for active/pending owner sessions, active transactions, pending operations, lifecycle ACTIVE and backend ownership, but remove credential vault readability from that ownership assertion.

Make credentialVaultRecovery enumerate destination and legacy refs per-ref, preserving readable refs, replacing matching unreadable destination refs when a readable legacy source exists, and reporting unrecoverable refs without one corrupt row poisoning unrelated recovery.

Move the Graphiti Neo4j credential provisioning decision into a narrow testable module and regenerate only GRAPHITI_NEO4J_CREDENTIAL_REF when its persisted value fails with CREDENTIAL_VAULT_DECRYPT_FAILED or CREDENTIAL_VAULT_ENTRY_CORRUPTED; propagate CREDENTIAL_VAULT_SECURE_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE and all unrelated failures unchanged.
Add direct regressions for the fresh-process owner-free/unreadable-vault boundary, per-ref unreadable recovery, and exact Graphiti-only regeneration policy.
